summary: Of Rivers and Religion is a 1972 album by American folk musician John Fahey, credited to John Fahey and His Orchestra. It was his first release on a major label, Reprise Records, and marked a major departure from his earlier work by adding a backing band and a Dixieland jazz style. Although Time named it one of the Top Ten albums of 1972, it was hard to market and drew little enthusiasm at Reprise.
